summary: Intermittent IdP metadata fetch timeouts causing token-exchange failures for private deployment (users unable to sign in)
description: Issue summary: Customers in a private VPC configuration report intermittent sign-in failures across the eu-west region. Impact: A subset of end-users cannot complete OIDC sign-in; sessions fail during token exchange and downstream model inference calls are blocked. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) with Redwood Private control plane in eu-west. Identity traffic egresses via a shared NAT gateway. Observed behavior: When the customer's IdP metadata endpoint returns 5xx or times out, Redwood's identity-proxy fails token exchange and surfaces 403/502 to the client with logs containing 'token_exchange_failed: metadata_fetch_error'. Expected behavior: Identity-proxy should gracefully retry metadata fetch and fallback to a recently cached metadata/JWKS blob to avoid user-facing failures. Steps to reproduce: 1) From a host in the customer's private deployment, curl the IdP discovery endpoint: curl -v https://idp.finlyx.example/.well-known/openid-configuration 2) Simulate transient 503 responses (or block egress) and attempt OIDC sign-in flow via the Redwood private authentication proxy 3) Observe token-exchange failures and 5xx/403 responses in the client. Relevant logs/traces: identity-proxy error stream shows repeated 'metadata fetch failed, status=503' followed by 'token_exchange_failed'. Nginx upstream logs show 502 responses proxied to identity-proxy. Initial hypothesis: The identity-proxy does not have robust retry/backoff for discovery/JWKS fetch under transient IdP outages and the JWKS cache TTL/eviction policy is too aggressive in the private control plane, so a brief IdP outage causes widespread sign-in failures until cache repopulates. Temporary NAT gateway egress saturation may exacerbate the issue.

investigation_notes: Checked identity-proxy logs (instance id ip-10-1-4-23): repeated errors: 'GET /.well-known/openid-configuration -> 503', timestamp aligned with customer-reported window.
Captured nginx access logs: multiple proxied 502 responses to clients; upstream identity-proxy returned 502 after failing token exchange.
Verified JWKS cache TTL configured at 2m for this private tenant; cache eviction coincided with the outage window leading to immediate metadata refresh attempts.

Replayed token-exchange sequence against a mock IdP returning 503: identity-proxy attempted 3 immediate fetches with no exponential backoff and then failed the exchange path, returning 403 to the client.

Network telemetry: NAT gateway CPU and connection counts showed short-lived spikes but not full exhaustion; no packet drops at firewall level. IdP provider reported brief partial outage on their side.
Trace context: trace id 7a1b3c shows token-exchange path 95% of latency spent waiting on metadata fetch timeout (30s).
resolution: Mitigation/Workaround: increased metadata fetch retry attempts and added short exponential backoff; extended JWKS cache TTL to 30 minutes for the affected tenant and populated a last-known-good metadata blob in the private control plane storage. Permanent fix: engineering is implementing improved fetch resilience (exponential backoff, circuit-breaker, local persisted fallback) and will deploy to private control plane in next patch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2147). Owner: Samir Gupta. Follow-ups: update runbook with steps to manually inject cached metadata, add monitoring alert on metadata fetch error rate, and coordinate with customer to validate egress stability. Status: Patch in review and canary scheduled, awaiting rollout
